verses.text: Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me."
Balak did what Balaam said, and the two of them offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. I will tell you whatever he shows me." Then he went off to a bare hilltop.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have prepared seven altars, and on each one I have offered a bull and a ram."
The LORD put a message in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."
So Balaam went back and found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with all the leaders of Moab.
Then Balaam spoke his message: "Balak brought me from Aram. The king of Moab brought me from the eastern mountains. 'Come,' he said, 'put a curse on Jacob for me. Come, speak against Israel.'
But how can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I speak against those whom the LORD has not spoken against?
From the tops of the rocks I see them. From the hills I watch them. They are a people who live apart. They do not think of themselves as one of the nations.
Who can count the people of Jacob? They are as many as the specks of dust. Who can count even a quarter of Israel? Let me die like those who do right. Let my end be like theirs!"
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, but you have done nothing but bless them!"
Balaam answered, "Must I not be careful to say only what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Then Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will see only part of them, not all of them. From there, curse them for me."
So Balak took him to the field of Zophim on top of Mount Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there."
The LORD met Balaam, put a message in his mouth, and said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."
So Balaam went back and found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with the leaders of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"
Then Balaam spoke his message: "Get up, Balak, and listen. Hear me, son of Zippor.
God is not a human being, that he should lie. He is not a man, that he should change his mind. Does he promise and not do it? Does he speak and not make it happen?
Look, I have been told to bless. God has blessed, and I cannot change it.
He has not found any wrong in Jacob, or seen any trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them. They shout to welcome him as their King.
God brought them out of Egypt. He is like the strength of a wild ox for them.
No magic spell can work against Jacob, and no fortune-telling can harm Israel. Now people will say about Jacob and Israel, 'Look what God has done!'
Look! The people rise up like a lioness. They get up like a lion. They will not rest until they have eaten their prey and drunk the blood of what they have killed."
Then Balak said to Balaam, "If you won't curse them, at least don't bless them!"
But Balaam answered Balak, "Didn't I tell you that I must do whatever the LORD says?"
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps God will be pleased to let you curse them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Mount Peor, which looks out over the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me."
Balak did what Balaam said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
